Chapter 10: Sustaining Joy, Play, and Creativity in Relationships
When we talk about ethical non-monogamy, it’s easy to focus on the serious stuff—like communication, boundaries, and doing the emotional heavy lifting. But let’s not forget—relationships aren’t just about working through tough moments. They’re also meant to be a source of joy, inspiration, and fun.
So, what does it actually mean to sustain joy? Well, it’s about carving out time for adventures, laughter, and little moments worth celebrating together. Maybe it’s planning a special date, trying something totally new as a group, or just enjoying those everyday connections that make your heart feel lighter. Playfulness isn’t just about having a good time—it can smooth over tension, spark intimacy, and remind you why you’re on this journey in the first place.
Now, let’s talk about creativity. In non-monogamous relationships, you’ll often find you need to get a little inventive—coming up with fresh ways to show love, solve problems, or figure out how to spend time together. Embracing that spirit of experimentation? It can make your relationships stronger and way more rewarding.
So, how do you actually nurture joy and creativity? Here are a few ideas:
Start with shared rituals. Maybe that’s a weekly dinner, a regular game night, or picking up a hobby together—anything that brings everyone closer.
Don’t forget to celebrate milestones. Whether it’s an anniversary, a big achievement, or even a new chapter for someone in your group, mark the occasion with a meaningful gesture or a fun gathering.
Get curious and explore together. Try out something new—a trip, a creative project, or learning a new skill as a team.
And above all, keep expressing appreciation. Take a moment to notice and celebrate what each person brings to the table—their quirks, their support, their unique magic.
Picture this: a polyamorous family throwing a monthly potluck, where everyone brings their favorite dish and stories from the month. Or maybe a couple curates a playlist that captures the ups and downs of their journey together. It’s these little acts of creativity and celebration that help keep the connection alive.
When you make play and creativity a priority, you’re not just surviving—you’re keeping your relationships vibrant, uplifting, and full of life, even when things get tough.
